newsitem.title: INDIA: One killed, 11 injured by bus, taxi bombs in Delhi.
newsitem.headline: One killed, 11 injured by bus, taxi bombs in Delhi.

text.p: Two bombs, one in a bus and the other in a taxi, exploded minutes apart in the Indian capital on Saturday, killing one person and injuring at least 11, police said.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the explosions, which occurred in the Samaipur Badli area, about 25 km (15 miles) northwest of the centre of Delhi. Police said both bombs were crude devices.

Police said 12 people were taken to hospital, seven from the taxi and five from the bus. One passenger died in hospital and two were in a serious condition, deputy police commissioner Prabhap Singh told Reuters.
The first bomb exploded in a state-owned bus at around 5 p.m. (1130 GMT), damaging the inside of the vehicle and shattering its windows, witnesses said.

"When the bus left the Delhi bus terminal, there was a plastic jar inside a bag which the conductor saw and asked if it belonged to anybody," Rishi Ram Kaushik, who was travelling in the bus when the device exploded, told Reuters.
"No one replied, so it was kept behind the driver's seat," he said. The bus had about 60 passengers and was travelling from New Delhi to Sonepat in neighbouring Haryana state, police said.
The second explosion rocked the taxi minutes later some three km (two miles) away, police said. The jeep taxi was also heading to Sonepat and carrying about 10 people, Singh said.
The taxi was destroyed in the blast, its wreckage spattered with blood. Police with sniffer dogs later combed the area for clues.
At least 31 people have been killed in three separate bomb attacks in the capital over the past year. Police suspect Kashmiri or Sikh militants are responsible.

Saturday's blasts came a day after a bomb in a scooter taxi exploded near the home of the chief minister of northern Jammu and Kashmir state, killing seven people. The chief minister, Farooq Abdullah, was out of the country.
Jamait-ul-Mujahideen, a militant Kashmiri separatist group, claimed responsibility for the blast in a high-security area of the Kashmir valley's largest city, Srinagar.
Last Monday, two bombs exploded on a railway track in northeast India, ripping through a train and killing at least 33 people.
Bodo tribal militants fighting for a separate homeland in Assam state claimed responsibility for the attack.
